items.text: All required data already exists on the API response (HeartbeatConfigResponse at scenarios/prompt-manager/api/heartbeat/models.go:9-22): Enabled, LastExecution.Status/StartedAt, NextExecution, NextExecutions. The bug is purely a CLI human-output formatting gap at scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/teams/teams.go:1535-1539. No API schema change is required for the core fix.

Initiative neighborhood check: the other open members of prompt-manager-decision-workflow-polish (decision-show-options-default-output, decision-accept-no-options-ergonomics, decision-accept-initiative-proposal-auto-create) all touch the decision CLI/API, not heartbeats. No scope overlap. The three-surface parity rule from the initiative description still applies — UI heartbeat view should mirror the new labels.

items.context: What exact label tokens should the human output use? Tradeoff: terseness (single-segment label) vs. precision (compound label that always shows enable/disable + lifecycle). The description suggests `[enabled/scheduled]`, `[enabled/dormant]`. Open question: do we want the explicit `enabled/` prefix when the lifecycle word already implies enabled?

options.label: Compound: [enabled/scheduled], [enabled/active], [enabled/dormant], [enabled/broken], [disabled]
options.rationale: Operator-suggested form in the item description. Reading any line tells you both axes (toggle state + lifecycle) without reasoning. Slightly longer.

options.label: Single-token: [scheduled], [active], [dormant], [broken], [disabled]
options.rationale: Shorter; lifecycle word implies enabled (only `disabled` means off). Risk: easier to misread `disabled` as just another lifecycle state.

items.context: An enabled heartbeat with past fires is 'dormant' when... what? Pure wall-clock thresholds break for naturally-slow schedules (weekly cron). The classifier needs a deterministic, schedule-aware rule. NextExecution is already computed by the API and is in the response.

options.label: NextExecution in the past (now > NextExecution) — scheduler should have fired but didn't
options.rationale: Schedule-aware by construction; uses an already-computed field. If the next fire was supposed to happen and hasn't, something is wrong. Simple, deterministic, no tunable threshold.

options.label: LastExecution.StartedAt older than 2× the next-fire interval
options.rationale: Catches schedules that fire but with degraded cadence. Requires computing the interval; more complex; needs the schedule parser.

options.label: Fixed threshold (e.g., 24h since last fire)
options.rationale: Simplest. Wrong for weekly/monthly schedules — would flag healthy weekly heartbeats as dormant.

items.context: If LastExecution.Status is 'failed'/'error'/'timeout', is that always 'broken', or only 'broken' when the failure is recent? An old failure followed by long silence could be either label.

options.label: Status of the most recent execution decides — failure-status → broken regardless of age; non-failure-status + dormancy condition → dormant
options.rationale: Simple precedence: failure dominates. Operator sees 'broken' the moment it breaks and keeps seeing it until a successful run replaces the last execution.

options.label: Broken only if failure is recent (within dormancy threshold); old failure with silence → dormant
options.rationale: Treats long-stale failures as 'we don't really know any more'. More nuanced but more rules.

items.topic: Where to place the classifier function
items.context: The lifecycle classifier is logic the UI also needs (three-surface parity). Options for code placement.

options.label: In cli/teams/ (Go) and re-implemented in ui/src/ (TS), with a shared test-case fixture file (JSON) consumed by both
options.rationale: No new shared package; each surface owns its rendering. Shared fixtures keep the truth tables aligned. Lowest plumbing overhead.

options.label: In a new shared Go package consumed only by the CLI; UI re-implements independently
options.rationale: Cleaner Go boundary but UI still duplicates. No real win over A.

options.label: Compute the lifecycle state on the API side and add a `lifecycleState` field to HeartbeatConfigResponse
options.rationale: Single source of truth; both CLI and UI render from a server-supplied label. Wider blast radius (API contract change) but eliminates drift entirely.

items.context: The initiative's three-surface parity rule says all work ships across API + CLI + UI. The heartbeat UI surface needs verification — it may already display different fields, or there may be no equivalent list view yet.

options.label: Mirror the new labels in the UI heartbeat list view as part of this fix
options.rationale: Honors the parity rule; ships a coherent operator experience in one cut. Adds UI work scope.

options.label: Ship CLI-only now; file a separate fix item for UI parity
options.rationale: Smaller PR, faster CLI relief for the prep-agent walk pain point. Risks the UI item lingering and breaking the parity rule de facto.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: e.g., audit UI first, then decide.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with problem statement, scope (in/out + three-surface check), proposed lifecycle state model with rendering table, phased approach (classifier → CLI render → UI parity → docs), explicit test plan, risk register, and decision log placeholder. All five major decisions surfaced as workshop items d1-d5; one info item documents that the API already carries the data and another documents the initiative neighborhood check.
